Offset: Buch und Werbekunst, Bauhaus issue

A printing-trade magazine hands its 1926 issue to the Bauhaus, and Joost Schmidt answers with color bands, a black quarter-disc, and concentric rings.

Source
Harvard Art Museums: Offset: Book and Advertising Art, Vol. 7, Special Issue on the Bauhaus
Creator
Joost Schmidt
Made
1926
Style
Bauhaus (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Bold, constructive, geometric
Evidence
Downloaded and inspected the Commons scan (421 × 535 px). The scan is small, so fine print is only partly legible.
Reviewed
25 September 2026
Rights
Open license, stored. License: public domain. Rights policy

Context

Harvard Art Museums catalogues the cover under Joost Schmidt, 1926, “letterpress and offset lithograph with silver ink on paper,” 30.8 × 23.3 cm, object 2021.170. Harvard 372865.

Letterform Archive lists it as Offset: Buch und Werbekunst, Bauhaus-Heft, vol. 3, no. 7, Leipzig, 1926, with Joost Schmidt as cover designer. Letterform Archive. MoMA also holds a copy. MoMA 130203.

Observed

  • A yellow vertical band runs down the left edge; a gray field fills the right side.
  • A large black circle segment, with a stippled yellow edge, fills the upper middle.
  • Concentric rings in red, blue, yellow, and black spread from a small blue and white center at upper right.
  • “OFFSET” is set in very heavy red sans-serif capitals; “BUCH UND WERBEKUNST” is in white capitals on a blue band; “HEFT 7” and “1926” are on a black and a white band below.
  • Small vertical type at the right edge reads “BAUHAUS-HEFT” and credits the design to Joost Schmidt, Bauhaus in Dessau.

Why it belongs

The cover uses every item of the Bauhaus rubric at once: red, yellow, and blue as flat areas, circles as composition elements, heavy sans-serif, and bands that divide the page.

The concentric rings add optical movement, which links Schmidt’s cover to Bauhaus color and form teaching.

Borrow

Stack the masthead on horizontal color bands of different heights.

Use one large circle segment as the main image instead of a picture.
